public_rationale: Companies and survey respondents had reported financial benefits from AI. Lloyds reported GenAI value for 2025, while Deloitte recorded claims that benefits exceeded costs. Those records matter, but they do not supply the matched spending and realized bottom-line return required by the quoted wording. The search therefore neither establishes a decisive counterexample nor supports the universal claim.
limitations: A reading that accepts a reported financial benefit without corresponding expenditure would produce a different assessment.
Company-reported savings need not equal audited net returns.
The search is not a census of every company disclosure.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: No company has shown a clear bottom-line return on its AI spending.

statement.excerpt: Nobody — not a single company — has been able to express in clear-set terms based on their actual bottom line a conversion of “I spent this much money and got this in return.”

from_speaker: based on their actual bottom line
I spent this much money and got this in return
our_interpretation: The surrounding discussion concerns enterprise generative AI and LLM adoption, rather than every historical application of machine learning.
The ordinary reading requires a public, quantified connection between AI spending and realized financial benefit after relevant costs.
The present-perfect wording covers disclosures made by publication, with no stated starting date. This is a cumulative historical claim, not just a claim about the latest quarter.
A credible company disclosure can count without a separate audit, but projected savings, hours saved, and gross benefits without corresponding costs are insufficient.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence comprehensively establishes that no company had publicly supplied a quantified, attributable spending-to-realized-financial-return account by May 26, 2026.
criteria.contradiction_condition: At least one company had publicly quantified relevant generative-AI expenditure and the corresponding realized bottom-line benefit by May 26, 2026.
